BEYOND EARTH

Stand on the surface. Find the machines NASA left behind, then open their stories. Drag to look, scroll or pinch to zoom, WASD to walk.

Terrain is procedural (generated by code), not real NASA elevation data. Marker positions are schematic. Mission facts come from NASA records.

Mission Stories

Six machines, six endings. Each one was left behind for a reason. Press play to hear two of them tell their own story in Arabic, with English subtitles.

Trace every claim to its source.

We prioritize NASA mission pages, NASA image and data archives, and peer-reviewed research. A source link is a starting point for verification, not a substitute for checking the exact claim, date and mission context.

About Us

Echoes Beyond Earth is an interactive storytelling archive created by Team Odyssey for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We bring attention to the human-made objects that remain on the Moon and Mars, and the scientific stories they continue to tell.

Our mission

Turn forgotten mission hardware into accessible stories that help people understand the history and continuing value of space exploration.

Our approach

Combine storytelling, interactive exploration and reliable references so visitors can move from curiosity to evidence.

Our vision

Encourage a new generation to see the Solar System not as an empty landscape, but as a record of discovery, engineering and human ambition.

Every footprint leaves a trace.

Some objects were intentionally left behind as scientific instruments. Others became silent witnesses after their missions ended. Their stories deserve to be explored, documented and remembered.
